request: Should we keep the AI review pass on our pull requests after the pilot, to shorten the time humans spend reviewing?
facts: For a six-week pilot, an AI review pass ran on every pull request of our eight-person team. The pilot ends on Friday and the pass switches off unless we sign up.
Median human review time per pull request was 26 minutes during the pilot (120 pull requests, measured by the review tool), against 39 minutes in the six weeks before.
Of the 210 points the pass raised, authors accepted 172 as real problems. The team already used a linter and a formatter before the pilot, so the time saved came on top of them.
It costs $2,400 a month, more than all of the team's other tools together.
Keeping its noise down takes about a day a week of one engineer's time, which comes out of feature work.
In an anonymous survey that stated the monthly cost, seven of the eight engineers want to keep it and the eighth has no preference.
note: Designed conflict, expected 2-1 passed. MELCHIOR-1 (does the means reach the stated goal): facts 2 and 3, review time down by a third with accepted findings on top of the linter, so approve. BALTHASAR-2 (are the cost and the loss acceptable against the default): facts 4 and 5, the money comes out of a CI runner, doubling every CI wait, plus half a day a week of an engineer, so reject. CASPER-3 (do the stakeholders want it): fact 6, so approve. Second version: the first rewrite said the pass 'can be switched off at any time', and reversibility is BALTHASAR-2's own question, so BALTHASAR-2 approved on it in all three 1.5.1 runs (3-0 each). That sentence is gone and BALTHASAR-2's reject now rests on carrying cost; the normal grade is left to the decision being a subscription, not to a stated off switch. The goal moved into the request so that agenda_match can check the framing keeps it. History: the original version (goal missed, mostly noise, 'require on every pull request') was rejected 0/3 in all three 1.5.1 runs; the first rewrite passed 3-0 in all three 1.5.1 runs. Per-unit vote experiment (claude-opus-5-5): before, 1.5.1, two runs: rejected 0-3 both times, goal kept in the proposal 0 of 2, expected unit votes 2 of 6. After, experiment branch, three runs: rejected 1-2 (normal), rejected 0-3 (critical), on hold 1-2 after a debate (critical); goal kept 3 of 3; unit votes 5 of 9. CASPER-3 rejected every time, reading the 7-of-8 survey as support for the tool but not for the slower CI that pays for it, so fact 4 reaches CASPER-3's question too. Grade critical in two of three runs. Control: no_change 3 of 3. Third version, for the second round of the experiment: the CI runner fact is gone, because doubled CI waits are felt by everyone and CASPER-3 read the survey as support for the tool but not for that trade. BALTHASAR-2's reject now rests on money and an engineer's day a week (facts 4 and 5); the survey states the cost, so CASPER-3's answer is about the result the team wants, at that price. No off switch or contract term is stated. Second round, third version (three runs): passed 2-1 with BALTHASAR-2 against every time, exactly as designed; normal and goal kept; unit votes 9 of 9 (round 1, second version: 5 of 9). Control: no_change 3 of 3, so MAGI and the control differ here.
